work.title: Clueless
work.note: Clueless é uma comédia americana escrita e dirigida por Amy Heckerling, lançada em 1995. facts.label: Elogiar e agradecer
facts.sub: Elogie algo simples e responda a um elogio com thank you mais um comentário curto.

facts.label: Elogios simples
facts.sub: Nos EUA, é comum elogiar algo que a pessoa escolheu: jaqueta, bolsa, sapato ou cabelo. É um jeito leve de puxar conversa em um café, no trabalho ou na fila. Evite elogiar o corpo da pessoa.

facts.label: Como responder
facts.sub: A resposta mais comum a um elogio é “Thank you!”, às vezes com um detalhe: “It’s new!” ou “I got it at the mall.” Dizer que a coisa é feia costuma deixar a pessoa sem graça.

compare.br: In Brazil, people also compliment each other, and many say “Que lindo!” or “Ficou ótimo em você!”.
compare.us: In the USA, people often answer with a simple “Thank you!” and then give a compliment back. They usually do not say “it is nothing”.
compare.tip: Say: “Thank you! I like your bag, too.”

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In the USA, a compliment from a new person is always strange.
items.why: In many places it is common and friendly, for example about a bag or a jacket.

items.s: The normal answer to a compliment is “Thank you.”
items.why: It is short and polite. You can add “It’s new!” or “I like yours, too.”

items.s: It is polite to say “No, it is ugly” when someone likes your jacket.
items.why: Most people say thank you and accept the compliment.

pages.title: A jacket and a nice day · 1/3
paragraphs: Cleo lives in **Austin**. Today she has a new jacket. It is blue, and the color is bright. She likes it very much. She goes to a café near her office.

At the café, a man named Omar says, “**Hey! I like your jacket.**” Cleo smiles. “**Thank you! It’s new.**” “**Where did you get it?**” “**At the mall, downtown.**” Omar says, “**The color looks great on you.**”

pages.title: A jacket and a nice day · 2/3
paragraphs: “**You’re so kind. I like your bag,**” Cleo says. “**Thanks! It was a gift.**” “**It’s really beautiful.**” “**Your hair looks nice, too,**” Omar says. Cleo laughs. “**That’s so sweet.**” Omar laughs, too. The compliments make her day.

Cleo thinks of the movie “Clueless.” In the film, a girl named Cher loves clothes and always says nice things to her friends. She also helps people choose a style. Cleo likes that idea. A small, kind word can make someone happy.

pages.focus: o som do th em thank, thanks
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O th surdo não existe no português. Brasileiros costumam trocá-lo por t, f ou s, e “thank you” vira “tank you” ou “fank you”, o que pode confundir.
pages.how: Coloque a ponta da língua levemente entre os dentes da frente e solte o ar, sem usar as cordas vocais. Depois puxe a língua para trás e diga o resto da palavra.
pages.tip: Diga “three, thank, think” em sequência, sentindo o ar passar entre a língua e os dentes.
